summary: Whole-repository readiness audit at 6f4ec3b85bcf4899f8c0a8eaa185de17b53abb8c. One medium validation-readiness gap: the approved deployment path does not run the repository test suites before Azure changes and deployment. Twelve current product/operational documents were reviewed; no PR context applies.

findings.title: Deployment does not gate on the defined test suites
findings.problem: The only deployment workflow is manually dispatched, installs dependencies, then proceeds through writer quiescence and provisioning to deployment without running `npm test`. The Docker build performs package builds, but does not run the API or browser test suites. Those suites are available through the root `test` script (`package.json:11-13`) and are recommended for checking the work at `README.md:57`, but a failing regression can therefore reach the approved deployment path without a test gate. Add the test command before the workflow's first Azure mutation, or provide an equivalent required CI gate.
findings.current_code:
run: npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
run: npm run deployment-gate -- quiesce
run: azd deploy web --no-prompt
findings.suggested_fix: Run `npm test` in the workflow before the first Azure mutation (and preferably add a pull-request CI job using the root validation scripts), so API and browser tests must pass before maintenance or deployment begins.

positive_changes: The Azure runbook explicitly documents the destructive initialization boundary, writer-exclusion limits, backup/restore expectations, and that live Azure acceptance remains unvalidated.
The repository exposes root typecheck, build, and API/web test commands, and the deployment image builds both workspaces.
testing_recommendations: Before deployment, run `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` from the repository root as documented in README.md:57.
recommended_actions: Add an automated test gate before deployment workflow mutations, or require equivalent passing CI checks before an approved deployment can proceed.
risk_assessment: Medium readiness risk: tests are defined and documented, but the approved deployment workflow does not execute them before it can modify Azure resources or publish the app.
